subject: Pricing proposal and tiered volume discounts for high-throughput hosted API
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: tiered pricing + rate card for >1B tokens/mo

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — our engineering team was impressed with the latency numbers and the KV cache approach. We're running some projections and need a clearer sense of economics if we were to move to a hosted API model at scale. A few questions to help us model costs: 

- Do you have a published rate card for hosted text-generation by token?
- What volume discount tiers do you offer for steady-state throughput (e.g., >100M, >500M, >1B tokens / month)?
- Any committed-use pricing (monthly minimums or reserved capacity) vs. pure pay-as-you-go?
- Are there separate charges for streaming vs. non-streaming responses or for long-context KV cache usage?

We're currently modeling a 300M–1.2B tokens/month range for Q3 depending on Pilots. If you can share a proposal or a draft rate card we can take to finance and procurement, that would be great.

Also, legal will want to understand typical terms around data retention and audit logs; happy to loop them in.

Best,
Tom
Tom Ellis
Head of Platform
Acme Analytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Avery Johnson <avery@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: tiered pricing + rate card for >1B tokens/mo

Hi Tom — great to hear from you and glad the demo landed. Attaching our current rate card (redwood_rate_card_v2.pdf) and a short note below to surface the main options — happy to jump on a call to walk through the numbers with your finance/eng leads.

Summary (hosted API):
- Baseline pay-as-you-go: $0.0009 / token (text-gen, standard model)
- Volume tiers (usage discounts off baseline):
  - 100M–499M tokens/mo: 10% discount
  - 500M–999M tokens/mo: 18% discount
  - 1B+ tokens/mo: 25% discount (or talk to sales for custom reserved pricing)
- Committed reserved capacity (Dedicated) available for predictable throughput — typically starts with a 12-mo minimum commitment and gives an additional 10–15% off the applicable tier depending on GPU class
- Streaming: no separate charge for streaming response delivery; charges are token-based. Long-context (KV cache) may influence recommended model variant and therefore effective token cost; we can model that for your workload.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Tell me which steady-state band you expect to operate in (conservative/expected/peak).
2) We can provision a draft SOW + usage commitment if you'd like reserved pricing.
3) Loop in Legal for standard data-retention and audit language — we provide SOC2 evidence + configurable retention windows for logs.

I'll let Rishi and Avery chime in on flexibility for an initial pilot credit or one-time onboarding discount.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_rate_card_v2.pdf (56KB)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Inquiry: tiered pricing + rate card for >1B tokens/mo

Marissa — quick internal note on levers if Acme goes toward 1B tokens/mo: 

- Our published baseline for hosted is $0.0009/token. For strategic accounts (platform companies) we can go deeper on volume: 25% at 1B is OK as a public-facing starting point.
- For a multi-year committed reserved contract we can layer another 8–12% (depending on required GPU class and burst policy).
- We should consider including a one-time onboarding credit (e.g., $10k) for migration costs and a 60-day pilot at a slightly better rate for first 30M tokens to prove economics.
- Margin check: assume 1B tokens steady-state, effective revenue at 0.0009 * (1-0.25) = $0.000675/token = $675k/mo gross. With reserved capacity costs and support, we must keep gross margin above 30% (finance target).

If Acme is price sensitive we can propose a blended rate for year 1 (e.g., $0.00072/token) with a contractual minimum. Otherwise, stick to tiered list price + reserved add-on.

Recommend offering the 25% public tier and then a custom reserved offer if they sign an annual commitment — document terms in the SOW and send to Legal.

-Rishi
VP Sales Operations

Subject: Proposal: tiered hosted pricing + optional reserved capacity (RDW-2026-0423)

Hi Tom — thanks for the patience while we pulled internal approvals. Based on the usage profile you outlined, here's a concise proposal you can share with Finance/Legal. I'm attaching the updated rate card and a simple mutual action plan (MAP) that maps milestones to procurement steps.

Proposal highlights:
- Baseline hosted rate: $0.0009/token
- Volume tiers (applied monthly, retroactive):
  - 100M–499M: 10% off baseline
  - 500M–999M: 18% off baseline
  - 1B+: 25% off baseline
- Conditional reserved option: 12-month commitment for a further 10% off the applicable tier. Example: 1B+ reserved effective rate = $0.0009 * 0.75 * 0.9 = $0.0006075/token
- One-time onboarding credit: $10,000 applied to first invoice for contracts signed before 2026-04-15
- Pilot program: 60-day pilot at a promotional blended rate of $0.0008/token for the first 30M tokens (aimed to validate latency and caching benefits)

Procurement/Legal note: standard SOW + Data Processing Addendum (DPA) attached in the DocuSign link. We provide SOC2 Type II reports and can scope data-retention settings in the contract.

Next steps:
1) If this looks good signal interest and we'll issue a draft SOW/Order Form for signature.
2) If Legal requests language edits, have them send redlines to contracts@redwoodinference.com — I'll track and escalate.
3) If you want, we can run a modeled cost sheet based on expected token mix (short prompts vs. long generation) — I can have Solutions Engineering produce that.
